config.title: Test Error Boundary

intro.title: Test Error Boundary
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a test for an Error Boundary component in React. You will learn how to simulate errors in a child component to verify that your Error Boundary catches and displays a fallback UI as expected. The core programming concept involves using React's Error Boundary lifecycle methods and writing unit tests with a testing library like React Testing Library. You will work with constructs such as try-catch simulation, mocking errors, and assertions to ensure the Error Boundary functions correctly. This hands-on practice will help you understand how to make your React applications more robust by testing error handling.
intro.usecase: Error boundaries are essential in production React applications where components can fail unexpectedly. In a financial dashboard, an error boundary prevents a single faulty stock chart from crashing the entire dashboard, allowing users to continue viewing other widgets. In an e-commerce product listing, if one product card fails to load due to malformed data, error boundaries ensure the rest of the products remain visible while showing a fallback UI for the problematic item. Testing these boundaries ensures your application gracefully handles failures without disrupting the user experience.

objectives: Construct a React Error Boundary component with lifecycle methods
Implement error handling logic to catch JavaScript errors in child components
Configure fallback UI that renders when an error occurs
Integrate the Error Boundary component into an existing component tree
Manipulate component state to control error display and recovery
Initialize test scenarios that trigger error conditions
Apply Error Boundary patterns to prevent application crashes

steps.title: Import React and create ErrorBoundary component
steps.instruction: Import React and create a class component called ErrorBoundary with constructor and render method.
steps.hint: Start by importing React, then define a class component named ErrorBoundary that extends React.Component. Include a constructor and a render method that returns null for now.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and create ErrorBoundary component
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a React class component skeleton ready to implement error boundary logic.
successCriteria: React is imported and a class component named ErrorBoundary is created with constructor and render method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported React and created a class component named ErrorBoundary with both constructor and render methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: import React and create a class component called ErrorBoundary with constructor and render method.

steps.title: Add error state to ErrorBoundary
steps.instruction: Inside the ErrorBoundary component, add a constructor method that initializes state with hasError set to false and error set to null.
steps.hint: In a class component, you can define a constructor to set the initial state. Use this.state = { hasError: false, error: null }.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorBoundary component will have a constructor that initializes the component's state to track error status.
successCriteria: ErrorBoundary has a constructor that sets initial state with hasError: false and error: null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a constructor, but make sure it sets this.state with both hasError and error properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ErrorBoundary component needs a constructor to initialize state. Try adding constructor(props) { super(props); this.state = { hasError: false, error: null }; }.

steps.title: Implement getDerivedStateFromError lifecycle method
steps.instruction: Inside the ErrorBoundary class, add a static method called getDerivedStateFromError that takes an error parameter and returns an object with error: true and errorInfo properties.
steps.hint: The method should be static and return a state update object when an error occurs.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorBoundary class now has a static getDerivedStateFromError method that returns an error state object.
successCriteria: getDerivedStateFromError is defined as a static method that returns an object with error state properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure getDerivedStateFromError is a static method that returns an object with error state properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add a static getDerivedStateFromError method inside the ErrorBoundary class that returns an object when an error occurs.

steps.title: Implement componentDidCatch lifecycle method
steps.instruction: Inside the ErrorBoundary class, add a componentDidCatch lifecycle method that takes error and errorInfo parameters.
steps.hint: The componentDidCatch method is called when an error is caught by the error boundary. It receives two parameters: the error object and an info object with component stack information.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorBoundary class will have a componentDidCatch method defined with error and errorInfo parameters.
successCriteria: The componentDidCatch method is added to the ErrorBoundary class with two parameters named error and errorInfo.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added the componentDidCatch method inside the ErrorBoundary class with two parameters: error and errorInfo.
steps.feedbackWrong: The componentDidCatch method is missing or incorrectly defined. It should be a method inside the ErrorBoundary class that takes error and errorInfo parameters.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering logic to ErrorBoundary
steps.instruction: Inside the ErrorBoundary class, add a render method that checks if hasError is true and returns a fallback UI with an error message. If hasError is false, return this.props.children.
steps.hint: Use a conditional (if/else or ternary) in the render method to decide what to display based on the error state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorBoundary component now has a render method that conditionally displays either an error message or the children components.
successCriteria: The render method is defined and uses conditional logic to return different JSX based on the hasError state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your render method properly handles both the error and normal cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The render method is missing or doesn't correctly conditionally render based on the error state.

steps.title: Create BuggyCounter component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named BuggyCounter that returns a <div> with the text 'Buggy Counter' inside.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name BuggyCounter and have it return JSX containing a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A BuggyCounter component is created that renders a div with the text 'Buggy Counter'.
successCriteria: BuggyCounter is defined as a functional component and returns a div containing the text 'Buggy Counter'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the BuggyCounter component, but make sure it returns a div with the exact text 'Buggy Counter'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The BuggyCounter component wasn't created correctly. Create a functional component named BuggyCounter that returns a div containing 'Buggy Counter'.

steps.title: Add error-throwing logic to BuggyCounter
steps.instruction: Inside the BuggyCounter component, add logic that throws an error when the counter reaches 5.
steps.hint: You can use a conditional statement to check if the counter value equals 5, then throw a new Error.
steps.expectedOutcome: The BuggyCounter component will throw an error when its counter reaches 5, simulating a component failure.
successCriteria: BuggyCounter contains a conditional that throws an Error when counter equals 5.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some logic, but make sure to throw an Error when the counter equals 5.
steps.feedbackWrong: The BuggyCounter component should throw an error when the counter reaches 5. Check your conditional logic.

steps.title: Add increment button to BuggyCounter
steps.instruction: Inside the BuggyCounter component, add a button element with the text 'Increment' and an onClick handler that increments a counter variable.
steps.hint: You'll need to create a counter variable using useState, then add a button that calls a function to update that counter when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: The BuggyCounter component should have a button that increments a counter when clicked, setting up the ability to trigger errors when the counter reaches a certain value.
successCriteria: BuggyCounter includes a button with 'Increment' text and an onClick handler that increments a counter state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the button element with 'Increment' text and the onClick handler that increments a counter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The BuggyCounter component doesn't yet have the required increment button. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Wrap BuggyCounter with ErrorBoundary
steps.instruction: Create an App component that returns the BuggyCounter wrapped inside an ErrorBoundary component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component renders BuggyCounter inside ErrorBoundary, enabling error boundary functionality.
successCriteria: App component is created and returns ErrorBoundary wrapping BuggyCounter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your App component returns ErrorBoundary with BuggyCounter as its child.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component should return ErrorBoundary wrapping BuggyCounter. Try again.

steps.title: Test the error boundary behavior
steps.instruction: In the App component, add a button that says 'Reset Error' which, when clicked, resets the error state by calling a reset function passed as a prop to the ErrorBoundary.
steps.hint: You need to add a button element with an onClick handler that calls a reset function. The ErrorBoundary component should receive a reset prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now includes a 'Reset Error' button that can reset the error state in the ErrorBoundary when clicked.
successCriteria: A 'Reset Error' button is added in the App component with an onClick handler that calls a reset function, and the ErrorBoundary component receives a reset prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the button has an onClick handler that calls a reset function and the ErrorBoundary component receives a reset prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset button or its functionality is missing. Ensure you add a button with an onClick handler that calls a reset function and pass it as a prop to the ErrorBoundary.
